abstract: A review of the Mayo Clinic experience with primary anterior mediastinal seminomas involved 17 patients who had pure anterior mediastinal seminomas and four who had mixed germ-cell tumors containing seminomas. At follow-up, of the 17 patients with pure anterior mediastinal seminoma, nine had no evidence of disease and eight had died of metastatic disease. Of the four patients with mixed germ-cell tumor containing seminoma, two were alive at follow-up and two had died of metastatic disease. In the group with pure anterior mediastinal seminoma, these factors seemed to have been associated with a greater potential for progression of disease: older than 35 years of age, presentation with fever, superior vena caval syndrome, supraclavicular or cervical adenopathy, and roentgenographic evidence of hilar disease.
abstract_ja: メイヨークリニックにおける原発性前縦隔セミノーマ17例（純粋型）と、セミノーマを含む混合型胚細胞腫瘍4例の経験をレビューした。フォローアップ時点で、純粋型17例中9例は無病、8例は転移性疾患で死亡していた。混合型4例中2例は生存、2例は転移性疾患で死亡した。純粋型では、35歳超、発熱、上大静脈症候群、鎖骨上または頸部リンパ節腫大、X線上の肺門病変が、病勢進行の可能性の高さと関連していた。
